Prealgebra · Lesson 10.1

Adding and Subtracting Cases

Solve this lesson →All lessons

Combinatorics is counting, and the hard part is rarely the arithmetic. It is deciding what to count and making sure nothing gets left out or counted twice. This lesson covers the two places that go wrong, off-by-one errors at the ends of a list and double counting when two groups overlap.

Problem
An apartment has residents on every floor from the 33rd to the 1111th, both included. How many floors have people on them?
Show a hint
  • This list is short enough to write out. Start at the 33rd floor and count up one floor at a time until you reach the 1111th, and do not forget to count the 33rd floor itself.
  • Subtracting 11−3=811−3=8 counts the steps you take going up, not the floors you land on. There is always one more floor than there are steps, because the floor you start on never got a step of its own.
  • Take 11−311−3 and then add 11 to put the starting floor back in the count.
Show the full solution
The floors with people are 3,4,5,6,7,8,9,10,113,4,5,6,7,8,9,10,11, which is 11−3+1=911−3+1=9​ floors. Subtracting alone gives 88, but that counts the steps you climb between floors. The 33rd floor never got a step of its own, so add it back.
Problem
A rocket countdown calls every whole number from 3030 down to 00, both included. How many numbers are called?
Show a hint
  • The numbers run from 00 up to 3030, and both ends are spoken out loud, so both ends get counted.
  • Subtracting 30−030−0 gives the size of the gap, but it misses one of the endpoints. This is the fencepost slip.
  • For a run of whole numbers from the smaller to the larger, including both, the count is the larger minus the smaller, then plus one.
  • Do not forget that 00 is a real number the announcer says. It is one of the called numbers, not a skip.
Show the full solution
The announcer says every whole number from 00 to 3030, both ends included, so the count is 30−0+1=3130−0+1=31​. Plain subtraction measures the gaps between numbers, not the numbers themselves. Counting 00 to 22 gives 0,1,20,1,2, three numbers, not two.
Problem
How many whole numbers are strictly between 11 and 5050, not including 11 or 5050?
Show a hint
  • The word between leaves out both ends, so 11 and 5050 are off the table. What is the smallest number you are actually allowed to pick, and what is the largest?
  • Once you drop the ends, you are picking from 22 up to 4949. Now you just need to count that run of whole numbers, both ends included.
  • Counting from 22 to 4949 including both is 49−2+149−2+1. Remember the plus one, so you do not come up short by one.
Show the full solution
Between leaves out both ends, so the choices run from 22 to 4949. That is 49−2+1=4849−2+1=48​ whole numbers. The plus one puts back the starting number, which the subtraction skips.
Key idea
Fencepost rule. The count of whole numbers from aa to bb, both ends included, is b−a+1b−a+1. The subtraction b−ab−a counts the gaps between the numbers, not the numbers themselves, and the +1+1 adds back the end you started on. Think of a fence with a post every foot. A 10-foot fence has 10 gaps but 11 posts, since both ends get one.
Problem
Lockers 11 through 200200 line a hallway. Every locker whose number is a multiple of 55 gets painted. How many lockers get painted?
Show a hint
  • The painted lockers are the multiples of 55 inside the range. What is the first one, and what is the last one?
  • These numbers are evenly spaced, stepping up by 55 each time. Find how many steps fit, then remember to add one for the starting locker.
  • Use (last - first) divided by the step, then +1+1. Watch the off-by-one so you do not undercount.
Show the full solution
The painted lockers are 5,10,15,…,2005,10,15,…,200, stepping by 55. The span is 200−5=195200−5=195, which holds 195÷5=39195÷5=39 steps, so the count is 39+1=4039+1=40​. The steps are the gaps between lockers, and the first locker takes no step to reach, so it needs its own +1+1.
Problem
A radio station plays every 4th rank from 9696 down to 44. How many songs does it play?
Show a hint
  • Going down does not change anything. The same counting idea works whether the list climbs or falls, so look at the first rank, the last rank, and the size of each step.
  • The countdown spans from 44 up to 9696, a gap of 96−4=9296−4=92, and each step is 44. Divide the gap by the step to count the steps, then watch out for the fencepost.
  • Steps and songs are not the same. After you find how many steps of 44 fit in the gap, add 11 to count both ends.
Show the full solution
The ranks played are 96,92,88,…,496,92,88,…,4. The span is 96−4=9296−4=92 and each step is 44, so there are 92÷4=2392÷4=23 steps and 23+1=2423+1=24​ songs. Counting a falling list works exactly like counting a rising one, and the plus one catches the song you start on.
Problem
On Maple Street the even-numbered houses 24,26,…,15024,26,…,150 sit on the sunny side. How many houses are on the sunny side?
Show a hint
  • The sunny-side houses are evenly spaced, going up by 22 each time. Spot the first one and the last one inside the range.
  • The first even house is 2424 and the last is 150150. Both ends count, so this is the fencepost idea again.
  • Count the gaps with (last−first)÷step(last−first)÷step, then add 11 for the house you started on.
Show the full solution
The sunny-side houses are 24,26,28,…,15024,26,28,…,150, stepping by 22. The span is 150−24=126150−24=126, so there are 126÷2=63126÷2=63 gaps and 63+1=6463+1=64​ houses. After 6363 jumps of 22 you land on house 150150, and you still have to count house 2424 where you started.
Key idea
Evenly spaced count. For multiples or any evenly spaced run, the count is last−firststep+1steplast−first​+1, the fencepost idea with wider gaps. Dividing the distance from the first term in range to the last by the step gives the number of gaps, then add 11 for the term you started on. Be careful. The width of a range does not decide the count. The ranges 1010 to 2020 and 1111 to 2121 are equally wide, yet the first contains three multiples of 55 and the second only two. So find the actual first and last multiple inside your range before you count.
Problem
You are 9th from the front and 15th from the back of a line. How many people are in the line altogether?
Show a hint
  • The 9 people from the front include you, and so do the 15 people from the back.
  • If you just add 9+159+15, you get counted once from the front and once from the back.
  • You are only one person, so subtract the one extra time you were counted.
Show the full solution
Adding gives 9+15=249+15=24, but you sit in both counts, so drop one copy of yourself. The line holds 9+15−1=239+15−1=23​ people. The front group ends at you and the back group ends at you too, so you get counted twice and the −1−1 undoes it.
Key idea
Line counting. If you are the ffth from the front and the bbth from the back, the line has f+b−1f+b−1 people. Adding ff and bb counts you once from each side, twice in all, so subtract 11 to undo the double count. The same correction applies when two counts include the same item. It is in both totals, so subtract it once. Being 6th from the front and 4th from the back means 6+4−1=96+4−1=9 people, not 1010.
Problem
1515 kids play soccer, 1212 play chess, and 77 play both. How many kids play at least one?
Show a hint
  • Watch out, the 7 kids who play both got counted once in the soccer group and once in the chess group. They were counted twice.
  • Add the two groups together first, then take away the overlap so nobody is counted twice.
  • At least one means soccer or chess (or both), which is 15+12−715+12−7.
Show the full solution
If we just add the two groups, 15+12=2715+12=27. But that counts the 77 kids who play both twice, once inside the soccer count and once inside the chess count. To fix the double count we subtract the overlap one time, so 27−7=2027−7=20. That gives the number who play at least one game, soccer or chess. 2020​
Problem
2222 kids signed up for archery, 1919 for swimming, and 3333 signed up for at least one. How many signed up for both?
Show a hint
  • If you just add 22+1922+19, every kid who signed up for both gets counted twice, once on each list.
  • That double count is exactly the kids in both. So 22+1922+19 is too big by the number of both.
  • The real total signed up for archery or swimming is 3333. Set the overcount equal to that and the leftover is the both group.
Show the full solution
Adding the lists gives 22+19=4122+19=41, but only 3333 kids signed up at all. The extra 41−33=841−33=8​ is what got counted twice. Anyone who picked both archery and swimming sits on each list, so the overcount is exactly the size of the both group.
Problem
At a 50-person reunion, 3232 drink coffee, 1919 drink tea, and 88 drink both. How many drink neither?
Show a hint
  • Start by counting how many people drink coffee or tea. You cannot just add 3232 and 1919, because the 88 who drink both would be counted once in each group.
  • Add the two groups and then take away the overlap once, so the coffee-or-tea count is 32+19−832+19−8. That removes the double counting.
  • Once you know how many drink at least one of the two, the neither group is just the whole reunion minus that count. Subtract from 5050.
Show the full solution
The coffee-or-tea count is 32+19−8=4332+19−8=43, subtracting the 88 who landed in both groups. Everyone else drinks neither, so that is 50−43=750−43=7​ people. Adding 32+1932+19 alone gives 5151, more than the whole reunion, which is a signal that the overlap got counted twice.
Key idea
Inclusion-exclusion. The number in AA or BB is ∣A∣+∣B∣−∣A∩B∣∣A∣+∣B∣−∣A∩B∣. Adding the two groups counts anyone in both twice, once in each total, so subtract the overlap once. The number in neither group is the grand total minus that count. When items are sorted two ways at once, arrange the four groups in a 2×22×2 table. Each row adds across to a side total and each column adds down to a bottom total. Both must agree with the grand total in the corner, so any missing cell can be found by subtracting the known cells from the row or column total they share.
Fun fact
The word tally comes from a notched stick. Medieval shepherds carved one notch per sheep, and some split the stick so each party kept half, the notches had to match up to prevent cheating.
Problem
A garden has 7070 plants. 4040 are flowering, 3030 are in the sunny corner, and 2222 are both. How many plants are non-flowering and in the shade?
Show a hint
  • Sort the plants two ways at once, flowering or not, and sunny or shady. A little 2 by 2 table with four boxes can hold every plant.
  • Start from the corner you know. 2222 plants are both flowering and sunny. Use the row and column totals to fill the cells around it by subtracting.
  • There are 4040 flowering plants and 2222 of them are sunny, so the rest of the flowering plants are in the shade. Do the same for the sunny column.
  • The plant you want sits in the box that is non-flowering and shady, the last cell left. Make the four boxes add up to 7070.
Show the full solution
Sort the plants into four boxes, flowering or not against sunny or shady. The flowering and sunny box holds 2222. Flowering and shady is 40−22=1840−22=18, and non-flowering and sunny is 30−22=830−22=8. All four boxes add to 7070, so the non-flowering and shady box holds 70−(22+18+8)=2270−(22+18+8)=22​. Inclusion-exclusion gives the same number. The plants that are flowering or sunny total 40+30−22=4840+30−22=48, and the rest, 70−48=2270−48=22, are in neither group.
Problem
How many two-digit numbers are divisible by 33 or by 55?
Show a hint
  • Count the multiples of 33 and the multiples of 55 separately. For each, find the first and last one in the range, then use the evenly spaced count where the count is (last−first)÷step+1(last−first)÷step+1.
  • Adding the two counts is not the final answer. Some numbers got counted in both lists. Which numbers are divisible by 33 and by 55 at the same time?
  • A number divisible by both 33 and 55 is a multiple of 1515. Count those, since each one was counted twice, and subtract that overlap once.
Show the full solution
The two-digit multiples of 33 run 1212 to 9999, so there are (99−12)÷3+1=30(99−12)÷3+1=30 of them. The two-digit multiples of 55 run 1010 to 9595, so there are (95−10)÷5+1=18(95−10)÷5+1=18. The numbers in both lists are the multiples of 1515, namely 15,30,45,60,75,9015,30,45,60,75,90, which is 66. That gives 30+18−6=4230+18−6=42​. Divisible by 33 and by 55 means divisible by 1515, and each of those six numbers got counted once in each list, so it comes off once.

Practice these ideas

Practice
Seats 55 through 2323 are all filled, both ends included. How many people are sitting in the row?
Show the solution
Seats 55 through 2323 number 23−5+1=1923−5+1=19​, so 1919 people are sitting. The subtraction alone gives 1818, which counts the steps from the first seat to the last and leaves out one end. Check it on seats 11 to 33, where 3−1=23−1=2 but three people are sitting.
Practice
A timeline poster marks one tick per year from 19901990 to 20242024, both ends included. How many ticks are on the poster?
Show the solution
One tick per year from 19901990 to 20242024 gives 2024−1990+1=352024−1990+1=35​ ticks. Subtracting alone counts the gaps between ticks, and a row always has one more tick than gap. From 19901990 to 19921992 there are three ticks, not the two that 1992−19901992−1990 suggests.
Practice
A scientist records the temperature at every whole degree from 1212 down to −4−4, both included. How many readings does she take?
Show the solution
The readings run from −4−4 up to 1212. The gap is 12−(−4)=12+4=1612−(−4)=12+4=16, so the count is 16+1=1716+1=17​ readings. Subtracting a negative adds, and the plus one is the usual fencepost fix. From 22 down to 00 there are three readings even though the gap is 22.
Practice
A vending machine restocks every slot whose number is a multiple of 66, from slot 11 to slot 100100. How many slots are restocked?
Show the solution
The restocked slots are 6,12,18,…,966,12,18,…,96, since 96=6×1696=6×16 and the next multiple 102102 is past 100100. The span is 96−6=9096−6=90, which holds 90÷6=1590÷6=15 steps, so the count is 15+1=1615+1=16​. The steps are the gaps between slots, so add one for slot 66 itself.
Practice
Odd-numbered jerseys 15,17,19,…,6715,17,19,…,67 hang on a wall. How many jerseys are there?
Show the solution
The jerseys step up by 22, so this is an evenly spaced count. The span is 67−15=5267−15=52, which holds 52÷2=2652÷2=26 steps, and the count is 26+1=2726+1=27​ jerseys. The steps are the gaps between jerseys, and you are already standing on jersey 1515 before taking any step.
Practice
Bins 50,100,150,…,90050,100,150,…,900 are audited. How many bins are audited?
Show the solution
The audited bins are 50,100,150,…,90050,100,150,…,900. The span is 900−50=850900−50=850, which holds 850÷50=17850÷50=17 steps, so the count is 17+1=1817+1=18​ bins. Steps count the gaps between bins, and there is always one more bin than gap.
Practice
A class calls 100,96,92,…,20100,96,92,…,20, dropping by 44 each time. How many numbers are called?
Show the solution
The list drops by 44 from 100100 down to 2020. The span is 100−20=80100−20=80, which holds 80÷4=2080÷4=20 steps, so the count is 20+1=2120+1=21​ numbers. Those 2020 steps are gaps between numbers, and 100100 starts the list before any step is taken.
Practice
The first multiple of 77 that is at least 2020 is 2121, and the last no more than 9595 is 9191. How many multiples of 77 lie in the range 2020 to 9595?
Show the solution
Since 2020 and 9595 are not multiples of 77, the list is 21,28,35,…,9121,28,35,…,91. The span is 91−21=7091−21=70, which holds 70÷7=1070÷7=10 jumps, so the count is 10+1=1110+1=11​. The ten jumps land on the ten numbers after 2121, so 2121 itself needs the extra +1+1.
Practice
A marching band is 1515th from the start of the parade and 1212th from the end. How many groups are in the parade?
Show the solution
Adding gives 15+12=2715+12=27, but the band sits in both counts. Take off the one duplicate and the parade has 15+12−1=2615+12−1=26​ groups. Counting from the start includes the band and counting from the end includes it again, so it lands in the sum twice.
Practice
You are 77th from the front and 77th from the back of a line. How many people are in the line?
Show the solution
Adding gives 7+7=147+7=14, but you are in both groups, so the line holds 7+7−1=137+7−1=13​ people. Check it straight. Six people ahead of you and six behind you make 6+1+6=136+1+6=13.
Practice
2222 students ate pizza, 1818 ate burgers, and 1111 ate both. How many ate at least one?
Show the solution
Adding the groups gives 22+18=4022+18=40, but the 1111 who ate both sit in each count. Remove one copy and 40−11=2940−11=29​ students ate at least one. An overlap always gets counted twice, so it comes off once.
Practice
2828 customers bought a taco, 2121 bought a burrito, and 3535 bought at least one. How many bought both?
Show the solution
Adding the lists gives 28+21=4928+21=49, but only 3535 customers bought anything. The excess 49−35=1449−35=14​ is the number counted twice, which is exactly the both group. Buying both puts a customer on each list, so the sum runs over the true total by the size of the overlap.
Practice
A pet show has 3030 cats and 2020 dogs. Of all entries, 2828 are short-haired and 1616 cats are short-haired. How many dogs are short-haired?
Show the solution
Every short-haired entry is either a cat or a dog, so the short-haired cats and short-haired dogs together make 2828. That leaves 28−16=1228−16=12​ short-haired dogs. The 3030 cats and 2020 dogs are extra facts this question does not need.
Practice
How many two-digit numbers are divisible by 44 or by 99?
Show the solution
The two-digit multiples of 44 run 1212 to 9696, so there are (96−12)÷4+1=22(96−12)÷4+1=22. The two-digit multiples of 99 run 1818 to 9999, so there are (99−18)÷9+1=10(99−18)÷9+1=10. A number divisible by both is divisible by 3636, and the two-digit ones are 3636 and 7272, an overlap of 22. That gives 22+10−2=3022+10−2=30​. Those two numbers appear in each list, so they get counted twice unless you subtract them once.
